newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. criticises Japan on business practice talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. criticises Japan on business practice talks.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday criticised Tokyo for setting preconditions for discussing business practices in Japan's photo film market.

In a statement obtained in Tokyo before its official release later today, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky criticised the Japanese government's response concerning the U.S. request for consultations based on a 1960 international accord on restrictive business practices.
Washington says Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd is carrying out such business practices to keep Eastman Kodak Co out of the Japanese market.
Japan has said it will respond to the request only if Washington agrees to discuss what it calls restrictive business practices in the U.S. photo-film market at the same time.

"A decades-old principle established in the GATT and WTO is that parties should accept a request for consultations in good faith and not link claims and counterclaims," Barshefsky said in the statement.
A U.S. embassy official told reporters that Washington has yet to formally respond to Japan's government on this issue.
"It (the American film market) is an open market where everyone can compete on fair basis," he said.
This U.S. request for consultations is one of three measures taken by Washington to resolve a dispute with Tokyo over opening Japan's photo film market.
"The measures put in place by the government of Japan are a textbook case of a WTO member circumventing its market access obligations," Barshefsky said in the statement.
Another of Washington's measures is the setting up on Wednesday of a dispute settlement panel at the World Trade Organisation.
The U.S. embassy official said: "We are very confident that the WTO (panel) will rule in our favour on this complaint."

The other step is a parallel WTO process by Washington, under a 1994 world trade accord on services, saying that Japan's laws on the development of large-scale retail stores also discriminate against foreign photo goods.
The embassy official said the United States has asked Japan to respond to this argument by November 19.
